subject: Request: Uptime safety harness — canary pin + auto-revert authorization
body:
From: Jake Robinson <jake.robinson@acme.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: planned model refresh impacting throughput — request for safety plan

Hi Nikhil,

We have a scheduled model refresh on Aug 1 that the ML team at Acme wants to push to production. The updated model reduces latency for 95th percentile in internal tests but introduces slightly higher variance under bursty loads. Our compliance team flagged that if the canary crosses our SLA for more than 5 minutes, we need an agreed fallback/pin plan.

Can Redwood provide a canary safety harness that:
- pins stable variant automatically if 95th% latency > 350ms for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows,
- supports an immediate manual pin by us, and
- has an automatic revert to the stable model if canary error-rate > 0.5% over a 5-minute window.

We need this behavior guaranteed in writing so procurement can sign off. Attachments: internal runbook (not attached here).

Thanks,
Jake
Ops Platform, Acme Payments

---
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Jake Robinson <jake.robinson@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: planned model refresh impacting throughput — request for safety plan

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Short summary: they require a canary safety harness with pin + auto-revert thresholds tied to latency and error metrics. They want this as an SLA-aligned carveout for the deployment window; procurement will not sign without explicit authorization from product/SRE.

Requesting: approval to grant a temporary SLO exception that allows canary to run with the following controls (details attached):
- Canary window: 5% of traffic, ramp to 20% over 15min
- Pin rule: immediate pin to stable variant if 95p latency > 350ms for 2 consecutive 1-min windows
- Auto-revert: revert to stable if error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5min OR if pinned manually
- Observability: automatic page to on-call and an audit log entry for every automatic action
- Rollout guard: an opt-out toggle for customer to pin from their console

Attachments: proposed-canary-config.yaml (contains exact thresholds + rollout plan), sla-exception-form.pdf (for legal/procurement).

Can Laura or Marissa sign off on the temporary SLO carveout for Acme? We should include the Dedicated SLO clause and limit to the Aug 1 deployment window (48h).

-Nikhil
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: planned model refresh impacting throughput — request for safety plan

Thanks for the summary. A few quick items before I sign:
1) Confirm the observability hooks will show per-variant 95th latency and error-rate to both Redwood and Acme in real-time (no >60s delay).
2) Ensure the auto-revert action is auditable and reversible only via an authorized ticket (no silent mask).
3) Limit the carveout to the Aug 1–Aug 3 window and include a hard stop at 72h unless we explicitly extend.

If Marissa confirms the runtime guarantees (1) and (2) I will approve the temporary SLO exception limited as above. If not, we route to emergency review.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: planned model refresh impacting throughput — request for safety plan

Confirmed: runtime guarantees are achievable with our Dedicated runtime and cloud-hosted offering if we enable the following controls (we've validated in staging):
- Metrics emitted at 15s granularity for per-variant latency and error-rate (satisfies real-time visibility).
- Automatic pin action is recorded in a rollback/audit log and emits a trace with an action id.
- Manual pin from customer console requires two-factor confirmation (audit requirement).
- We will add an outbound webhook to Acme's incident system when an automatic pin or revert occurs.

I will add a short paragraph to the sla-exception-form confirming the above guarantees and limit it to Aug 1 00:00–Aug 03 23:59 UTC (72h). After that window, the model rollout reverts to standard rollout policy.

Marissa Cole
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Jake Robinson <jake.robinson@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Approval: temporary SLO carveout for Acme Payments (canary pin + auto-revert)

Jake / Acme team —

Redwood approves the temporary SLO carveout for the Aug 1–Aug 3 deployment window subject to the controls listed below (we will attach the signed sla-exception-form after legal review):
- Canary window: start at 5% traffic, ramp to max 20% over first 15 minutes.
- Pin threshold: immediate pin if per-variant 95th latency exceeds 350ms for two consecutive 1-minute windows.
- Auto-revert threshold: revert to stable variant if canary error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5 minutes or following a manual pin.
- Observability: metrics at 15s granularity; automated webhook to Acme incident system on actions; audit log entries for all automatic/manual actions.
- Timebox: authorization valid 2027-08-01 00:00 UTC through 2027-08-03 23:59 UTC.

Please confirm receipt and that Acme's procurement will proceed; Nathan from legal will route the signed exception form by EOD.

Thanks,
Laura

Attachment stubs: proposed-canary-config.yaml (see Drive link), sla-exception-form.pdf (sent to legal).
